chunks: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام addressed the people and said: “Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, has set boundaries, so do not transgress them; and He has made obligations binding, so do not diminish them. And He was silent about certain matters—not out of forgetfulness regarding them—so do not burden yourselves concerning them, as a mercy from Allah for you; so accept it.”

Then ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Halal is clear, and haram is clear, and doubtful matters lie between that. So whoever leaves what is doubtful to him of sin, then he will be even more likely to leave what has become clear to him. And acts of disobedience are the sanctuary of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; so whoever grazes around it is about to enter it.”

key_terms.حُدُودًا: divinely set limits and boundaries that must not be transgressed
key_terms.حِمَى اللَّهِ: the protected sanctuary of Allah, which one must not approach unlawfully
key_terms.شُبُهَاتٌ: doubtful or ambiguous matters between clear permissibility and prohibition

ai.seo_question: What does Imam ʿAli عليه السلام teach about halal, haram, and doubtful matters?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that Allah has clearly laid down limits and obligations, while leaving some matters unmentioned as a mercy, not from forgetfulness. Imam ʿAli عليه السلام then warns believers to avoid doubtful matters, since staying away from ambiguities helps protect one from falling into clear sin.
